description: Is the Q_beta correction factor F required to be bar-even? No -- Q_A carries no bar parity to divide out, so bar-evenness of F is unsatisfiable, not merely un-required. Answers the open question at the end of bean qou-cds1.

data.Q_A_over_me: Mul(Integer(-1), Rational(1, 2), Pow(Symbol('q', positive=True), Integer(-3)), Add(Symbol('q', positive=True), Integer(1)), Add(Pow(Symbol('q', positive=True), Integer(2)), Mul(Integer(-1), Integer(2), Symbol('q', positive=True)), Integer(-1)))
data.domain_note: q^2-2q-1 < 0 at q0~1.11 and at its bar image 1/q0~0.901, so |.| resolves consistently on both sides
data.scope: (a) -- on the requirement as the chain states it, not a proof that no representation-theoretic argument could impose one
data.flagged_not_resolved: three-calibration-discipline-proof.md:33-36 and AGENTS.md:1937 call this same closed form 'the bar-odd (sinh) partner'; it is not bar-odd. Either the prose means the channel rather than the expression, or the two are inconsistent -- an owner call, not a symbolic one.

assertions.name: Q_A_is_not_bar_even
assertions.detail: bar(Q_A)/Q_A is not identically +1; it equals +1 only at q=1, where bar is the identity

assertions.name: Q_A_is_not_bar_odd
assertions.detail: bar(Q_A)/Q_A = -1 at no positive real q

assertions.name: no_power_of_q_restores_parity
assertions.detail: after stripping -q^3 the residue is a ratio of two distinct irreducible quadratics (roots -1+sqrt2, 1+sqrt2), not a monomial

assertions.name: F_bar_evenness_is_unsatisfiable_not_merely_unrequired
assertions.detail: F = Q_beta^exp/Q_A with Q_beta^exp bar-even trivially, so F's parity is Q_A's; Q_A has none, so no F multiplying it is bar-even
